title: 知覚・認知心理学B
subtitle: Psychology of Perception and Cognition B
educationalGoal: Through reflecting the students' daily cognitive activities and connecting them with the theories covered in the class, students will: - be able to understand the characteristics of human cognitive functions. - be able to grasp the mechanism of human cognition and thought, as well as impediments to them.
advice: This course will focus on the contents of cognitive psychology, which is a psychological area that captures human cognitive functions as information processing systems. Cognitive psychology has been developed by using a conceptual device called information processing (using a computer metaphor). Elucidation of human “intelligence” (cognitive characteristics of human information processing) is indispensable for the foundation of the realization of “intelligence” in machines such as artificial intelligence and robotics, which have attracted attention in recent years. Specifically, the following materials are covered. (1) Representation of knowledge and processing: (a) Declarative knowledge / Procedural knowledge, (2) Conscious processing and unconscious processing: (a) Attention, (b) Controlled processing and automatic processing, (3) Encoding processes and retrieval processes: (a) Memory, (b) Levels of processing, (c) False memory, (D) Defective memory,(4) Cognitive psychology in the real world. The above contents are learned through knowledge internalization (for example, lectures) and knowledge externalization (for example, report). We perform various cognitive activities in everyday life. It is desirable to understand the content of the course while being conscious of cognitive activities in daily life. Also, to deepen understanding of cognitive psychology, it is desirable to take Psychology of Perception and Cognition A that is offered separately. * Be sure to bring a computer each time as you will be using the e-syllabus. This subject is subject to the course credit system.
requiredKnowledge: It is desirable: to understand the contents of Educational and School Psychology and Practice of Elementary Psychological Experiments that were held in the separately. to set mastery goals to grow yourself, not performance goals to obtain a credit.

achievementLevels.ideal: (1) Understand the characteristics of human cognitive functions, express them in own words and consider about them. (2) Grasp the mechanism of human cognition and thought, as well as impediments to them, express them in own words and consider about them. (3) Understand situations where knowledge of cognitive psychology is utilized in the real world, and become able to increase perspectives on future career paths.
achievementLevels.standard: (1) Understand the characteristics of human cognitive functions and have your own thoughts. (2) Grasp the mechanism of human cognition and thought, as well as impediments to them and have your own thoughts. (3) Be aware of the future career paths , understand the situation where knowledge of cognitive psychology is utilized in the real world.
